question_text: A 2-month-old boy is brought to the pediatrician by his parents after they notice that he had a “floppy” appearance, poor suckling, vomiting, and spontaneous generalized movements a few weeks after birth. The boy was born at home, and routine newborn screening was normal. On physical examination, the infant is hypotonic, has poor suckling, cannot hold his head straight while prone, and does not follow objects. He has fair skin, red hair, blue eyes, eczema, and galactorrhea. At the second appointment, laboratory tests show high levels of phenylalanine and prolactin and low levels of homovanillic acid and serotonin. Which of the following enzymes is deficient in this patient?

Question: A 2-month-old boy is brought to the pediatrician by his parents after they notice that he had a “floppy” appearance, poor suckling, vomiting, and spontaneous generalized movements a few weeks after birth. The boy was born at home, and routine newborn screening was normal. On physical examination, the infant is hypotonic, has poor suckling, cannot hold his head straight while prone, and does not follow objects. He has fair skin, red hair, blue eyes, eczema, and galactorrhea. At the second appointment, laboratory tests show high levels of phenylalanine and prolactin and low levels of homovanillic acid and serotonin. Which of the following enzymes is deficient in this patient?

Options:
opa. Dopamine hydroxylase
opb. Phenylethanolamine N-methyltransferase
opc. Phenylalanine hydroxylase
opd. Dopamine decarboxylase
ope. Dihydropteridine reductase

The additional findings of high prolactin and low homovanillic acid and serotonin levels point towards a deficiency in the synthesis of neurotransmitters, which is characteristic of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) deficiency.
